radiology_report:
Tergooi MC
Department of Radiology
Date: 15 Feb 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation of rising PSA (7.7 ng/mL) in a 71-year-old male with prior biopsy-proven low-grade prostate cancer. Assessment for suspicious focal lesions.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume is 73.0 mL.
T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a heterogeneous peripheral zone. In the right apex, a 12 mm ill-defined hypointense area is noted. This region shows restricted diffusion on DWI (high signal on b=1400, low ADC) and early enhancement on DCE sequences. No extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or bone lesions within the field of view.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 3 lesion in the right apex peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 73.0 mL, PSA density 0.11 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.6079056.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient attended for routine monitoring. PSA measured at 2.6 ng/mL, which was within normal limits for his age. No urinary symptoms were reported at that time. Decision was made to continue annual PSA screening.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient returned for follow-up. PSA had risen to 4.5 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Given the PSA increase, a repeat PSA test was scheduled for three months later to assess velocity.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (oldest): The histological assessment reveals acinar growth pattern consistent with Gleason score 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, apex right.

Biopsy timepoint 2 (latest): The histological assessment reveals acinar growth pattern consistent with Gleason score 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, apex right.

Summary: The histological trajectory across timepoints is stable, with persistent ISUP grade group 1 disease.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 2.
